paper.title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with Large Language Models Enables Open-World Multi-Task Agents
paper.central_claim: DEPS - an event-triggered descriptor, an LLM that explains failures and re-plans, and a trained horizon-predictive goal selector - makes zero-shot LLM planning reliable for long-horizon open-world tasks: the first zero-shot multi-task agent that robustly accomplishes 70+ Minecraft tasks with nearly doubled overall performance, the first planning-based agent to reach diamond, and generally effective in ALFWorld and tabletop manipulation.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope: frozen LLM planner/explainer driving a learned visuomotor goal-conditioned controller of a simulated Minecraft agent, plus ALFWorld and a simulated UR5e tabletop (A-type harness, simulation only).

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method; MineDojo 30 runs per task, same BC controller; DEPS 48.56 vs CaP 25.77 (same code-davinci) but IM/CoT/GPT on text-davinci despite a 'same LM model' statement; selector and round ablations; demonstrations (wooden_button, stone_sword) are evaluated tasks; 'robustly 70+ tasks' and 'almost identical across LLMs' are contradicted by Tables 21/19; diamond 0.59% without denominator; tabletop DEP = GPT. Cross-domain instantiations are re-engineered per domain, so no transfer. Expected online, scoped.

signatures.object: Interactive re-planning loop around a zero-shot code-style LLM planner: descriptor -> explainer -> re-planner.
signatures.information: Initial plan is a Python-like program with per-step preconditions/effects; on failure the descriptor feeds back a text summary of plan-relevant symbolic game state (inventory, biome etc., game-provided); the explainer prompt sees the failed action and inventory.
signatures.operation: Controller runs goals sequentially; a failed goal triggers description d_t, LLM self-explanation e_t, and re-plan P_t over the accumulated dialogue prompt p_t = CONCAT(p_{t-1}, d_t, e_t).
signatures.output: Revised goal sequence passed to a goal parser and the goal-conditioned BC controller.
signatures.conditions: Rounds bounded by the LLM token window (about 7-8 for Codex); two few-shot DEP demonstrations; symbolic game feedback available.
signatures.feedback: game-provided inventory/event info translated to text; success detector from inventory changes
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable: single revised plan per round, no candidate pool.
signatures.persistence: within-episode dialogue only; nothing is kept across tasks.
signatures.claimed_effect: DEP (without selector) 39.36 average vs best baseline CaP 25.77; success rises monotonically with re-planning rounds (MT1 28.6 -> 79.8).
signatures.failure_boundary: Hard tasks MT6-MT8 (<=13.8%) limited by the BC controller; token window caps rounds.

signatures.object: Goal selector ranking parallel executable goals in the plan by predicted remaining horizon.
signatures.information: Current observation/state and candidate goal text; trained on offline trajectories (source and size of trajectories not stated in the paper text), backbone shared with the controller.
signatures.operation: Predict horizon distribution mu(h | s, g) and choose the goal with the smallest expected remaining steps (softmax over -mu).
signatures.output: Order/choice among parallel goals, modifying the plan.
signatures.conditions: Only when the plan contains alternative or order-free goals; limited episode length makes efficiency matter.
signatures.feedback: none at run time beyond the current state
signatures.selection_rule: argmax of exp(-mu(g,s)) over executable goals G_t.
signatures.later_use: used on each decision step of later tasks
signatures.claimed_effect: DEP 39.36 -> DEPS 48.56; +22.3 / +29.2 / +32.6 points over no selector at 2/3/4 parallel goals; beats CLIP/MineCLIP selectors.
signatures.failure_boundary: Needs a controller-aligned dataset; gains concentrated on efficiency-sensitive tasks (MT7).

gap.author_gap: (1) One-shot or weakly-corrected LLM plans fail on long open-world tasks needing 13+ ordered sub-goals; success-detector or scene-description feedback does not locate the plan error. (2) Plans ignore how reachable each alternative sub-goal is from the current state, making them infeasible or inefficient.
gap.checked_gap: Supported: Inner Monologue and other feedback planners are run on the same 71 tasks with the same controller and collapse from MT3 onward; DEPS ablations (rounds, selector variants) address each gap separately. Figure 1's oracle-controller evidence cannot be checked in text.
lineage: Zero-shot planner [16] / Chain-of-Thought [45] -> SayCan [4] (affordance), Code-as-Policies [20] (success detector, pythonic), ProgPrompt [42] (pythonic prompts), Inner Monologue [17] (scene descriptor + success detection) -> DEPS (precondition-annotated plan + failure explanation + horizon selector)
gap.closest_adjacent: Inner Monologue and Code-as-Policies re-implemented in Minecraft (IM on a weaker text-davinci LLM; CaP on the same code-davinci LLM).
gap.residue: Locating and repairing a wrong precondition in a long plan from execution feedback, and choosing efficient routes among equivalent sub-goals.
gap.stakes: Task completion within bounded episode lengths in open-world environments.
gap.method_response: Add failure descriptions, LLM self-explanation and re-planning, plus a learned reachability-aware selector.
gap.remaining_gap: Controller bottleneck on hard tasks (ObtainDiamond 60% with oracle vs 0.6% with BC); symbolic feedback unavailable on camera-only robots; explanation vs description not separated in Minecraft.
gap.current_relevance: Not assessed from later work; no later paper in the pinned local set bears on it.
unresolved: Figure 1 oracle-controller numbers are not in the pinned text.
Source and size of selector training trajectories are unstated.
gap.aggregate_note: Sol checked gap retained: explicit failure explanation and horizon-ranked parallel goals are the residual distinction; the claim that all prior planners assume a correct initial plan is too strong given Inner Monologue. Basis for G=3.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C25 step1 responsibility boundary: yes (LLM plans/explains; controller executes; selector scores). Step2 typed machine-checkable artifact: yes (code-style plan with preconditions/effects parsed to controller skills). Step3 close the loop with an obtainable signal mid-construction: yes (inventory-based success/failure plus description). Step4 ablate the loop: yes (rounds, selector variants; explanation only in ALFWorld). Step5 cost and confounds: cost absent, baselines on different LLMs, symbolic privileged feedback acknowledged.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: closed-loop signals obtainable by the system - partial (game symbols). Success: single load-bearing mechanism ablated to a named baseline - partial (DEP vs IM/GPT+RP confounded). Failure: cost of delegation unmeasured - present; failure: baselines re-implemented per benchmark - present; failure: only marginal over unified baseline - absent.
matches.reason: The operation is a planner/controller/selector decomposition around typed plan artifacts with execution-fed correction, which is the decompose-and-delegate move; the executor is a learned BC controller and the checker is an inventory predicate rather than a sound solver, so only partial.

rs_pattern.reason: Primary fit to decompose_and_delegate; conditioning few-shot demos are scaffolding and not the claimed mechanism, so no supporting card is added.

executes_pattern.reason: Plan artifact, execution feedback loop and a learned selector are implemented and ablated, but the explanation component is isolated only in a 10-task ALFWorld test.

resolves_problem.reason: Success on mid-difficulty tasks rises substantially (MT3-MT5) but MT6-MT8 stay at or below 14% and diamond at 0.59%; the controller, not the planner, is the limiting factor there.

pattern_mapping.conditions_and_differences: K202 assumes a completion/stagnation monitor; here the monitor is exact because it reads inventory, and the hand-back additionally triggers an LLM self-explanation that K202 does not describe.

claims.text: DEPS nearly doubles the success of existing LLM planners on 71 Minecraft tasks with the same controller.
claims.setting: MineDojo 1.11.2, empty inventory, behaviour-cloned goal-conditioned controller, 71 tasks in 8 meta groups, 30 runs per task
claims.baseline_control: GPT zero-shot, ProgPrompt, CoT, Inner Monologue, Code-as-Policies (author re-implementations; GPT/CoT/IM on text-davinci, PP/CaP/DEPS on code-davinci)
claims.selection_vs_test: Prompt design and two in-context demonstrations (wooden_button, stone_sword) come from the evaluated task family; selector trained on controller trajectories of unspecified origin.
claims.result_denominator: Average 48.56 (DEPS) vs 25.77 (CaP, same LLM), 21.64 (IM), 18.89 (CoT), 16.88 (PP), 15.42 (GPT); averages over 69 listed tasks (agg:E003), >=30 runs each; MT6-MT8: 13.80 / 12.56 / 0.59
counterevidence: MT6+ near zero so 'robustly 70+ tasks' is an overstatement
claims.allowed_conclusion: On the authors' Minecraft task suite and controller, DEPS roughly doubles the average success of the same-LLM best baseline (1.88x) and raises mid-difficulty tasks substantially; hard tasks remain largely unsolved.

claims.text: The horizon-predictive selector improves plan efficiency.
claims.setting: Minecraft with 2-4 parallel candidate goals; Task101 DEP vs DEPS
claims.baseline_control: fixed, random, MineCLIP, CLIP selectors; DEP (no selector)
claims.result_denominator: 39.36 -> 48.56 average; +22.3/+29.2/+32.6 points over no selector (curves only in figure)
claims.allowed_conclusion: A learned remaining-horizon ranker helps in this environment where parallel goals have different distances; transfer to other embodiments is untested.

claims.setting: Minecraft re-planning rounds 0..inf; ALFWorld GPT+RP vs DEP
claims.result_denominator: MT1 28.6 -> 79.8 with rounds; ALFWorld avg GPT+RP 52.0 vs DEP 76.0 (10 tasks x 5 runs)
counterevidence: ALFWorld feedback and admissible actions are privileged text
claims.allowed_conclusion: More feedback-driven re-planning rounds help monotonically; the extra value of the LLM's explanation beyond plain re-planning is supported only by a small ALFWorld test.

claims.text: DEPS is effective in non-open-ended ALFWorld and tabletop manipulation.
claims.setting: ALFWorld text world 10 tasks x 5 runs; CLIPort UR5e simulated tabletop 5 tasks x 5 seeds
claims.selection_vs_test: prompts and descriptors re-engineered per environment
counterevidence: tabletop shows no gain over zero-shot GPT
all methods get 0% on Pick Two
claims.allowed_conclusion: Small-scale simulated tests show gains in ALFWorld and parity in tabletop; not evidence of general effectiveness.

claims.text: First planning-based agent to reach diamond in Minecraft.
claims.baseline_control: cited RL/VPT/DreamerV3 numbers from other papers
claims.result_denominator: 0.59% (denominator not stated; not a multiple of 1/30); 60% with an oracle controller (denominator not stated)
claims.allowed_conclusion: A planner-driven pipeline reached a diamond in rare runs; the rate is far below prior imitation/RL systems and its denominator is unreported.

claims.text: DEPS based on different LLMs shows almost identical success rates.
counterevidence: Up to ~3x spread on hard meta-tasks
claims.allowed_conclusion: Contradicted by the paper's own table: DEPS improves over the vanilla planner on every LLM, but success is not nearly identical across LLMs.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulator success (environment-checked item acquisition) with repeated runs. No transfer: ALFWorld/tabletop use separately engineered harness instances (different LLM, descriptor, no selector) rather than the same harness on unused embodiments, tabletop tasks are CLIPort-seen with no gain, and demonstrations overlap evaluation tasks.
assessment.author_claim_preserved: DEPS - an event-triggered descriptor, an LLM that explains failures and re-plans, and a trained horizon-predictive goal selector - makes zero-shot LLM planning reliable for long-horizon open-world tasks: the first zero-shot multi-task agent that robustly accomplishes 70+ Minecraft tasks with nearly doubled overall performance, the first planning-based agent to reach diamond, and generally effective in ALFWorld and tabletop manipulation.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With a fixed behaviour-cloned controller and game-native symbolic feedback, DEPS raises average success on the authors' 69-task Minecraft suite from 25.8% (same-LLM CaP re-implementation) to 48.6% (38/69 tasks at >=50%, 16/69 at <=10%), with a selector gain of +9.2 and monotone gains from replanning rounds; 'robustly accomplishes 70+ tasks', 'almost identical across LLMs', 'general effectiveness' (tabletop parity) and the diamond milestone (denominator unreported) are not supported at the claimed strength.
unresolved: Explanation component isolated only in ALFWorld
baseline LLM mismatch vs stated 'same LM model'

G.reason: Resolved toward sol (son55 4). Two specific bottlenecks (repairing long plans after execution failure; controller-aware ordering of parallel goals) with Inner Monologue/CaP/ProgPrompt re-run on the same tasks. Not 4: the authors' framing that prior work assumes a correct initial plan is overstated (Inner Monologue already re-plans from feedback), the explanation-vs-feedback residual is not separated in the main domain, and the oracle-controller motivation (Fig. 1) is not checkable in text.

M.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Precondition-annotated plans support error localisation; explainer targets the stated cause; horizon selector targets reachability; rounds and selector make distinguishable predictions. Explanation value beyond plain replanning is argued but only tested in ALFWorld.

X.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Eq. (1), full prompts/dialogue, parser, inventory success detector, token-bounded rounds and controller details are given. Not 4: selector training data/size and candidate formation unclear; task bookkeeping inconsistent (71 claimed vs 69 table rows).

measurement.reason: Resolved toward sol (son55 3) under the anchors v2 clause 'criterion exists but denominator incomplete (some tasks with trial counts, some without) -> 2'. Programmatic inventory success with >=30 runs per task is strong for 68 tasks, but the headline ObtainDiamond 0.59% and the oracle 60% have no stated denominator (0.59% is not a multiple of 1/30), and the claimed 71 tasks do not match the 69 rows that the reported AVG is computed over.

causality.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 2). Same BC controller for all methods; CaP on the same code-davinci LLM gives the matched headline comparison (48.56 vs 25.77); selector isolated (DEP 39.36 vs DEPS 48.56) with fixed/random/CLIP/MineCLIP variants; round ablation from the vanilla planner; within-model vanilla-vs-DEPS on four LLMs; same-LLM GPT+RP vs DEP in ALFWorld. Remaining confounds: IM/CoT/GPT on a different LLM despite the 'same LM model' statement (agg:E004), DEPS demonstrations include replanning turns, explanation not isolated in Minecraft, extra rounds not budget-matched. Anchor 3: main controls adequate, some alternatives open.

holdout.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 1). Two in-context demonstration tasks (wooden_button, stone_sword) are evaluated tasks and Minecraft pretraining exposure is conceded, but the other 67 tasks were not demonstration tasks, worlds/spawns are randomised, and DEPS runs on two further Minecraft versions with different controllers (no baselines there). Auxiliary domains are re-engineered and the tabletop gain is 0. Anchor 2 (development overlap with evaluation; holdout gain ~0) rather than 1. The symbolic inventory/biome descriptor is game-native observation with a stated source, so anchor precedent 1 (unstated-source privileged state) is not applied as an extra deduction.

statistics.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). >=30 runs per task and a full per-task table, but the reported +- is dispersion across tasks within a meta-group, not run variance; no CI or paired test; no planner failure decomposition; ALFWorld/tabletop 5 runs without variance. Anchor v2: trial counts without variance/CI -> 1-2; per-task table supports 2.

cost.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 1). Step caps and controller are shared across methods and replanning is bounded at about 7-8 Codex rounds, so the LLM-call budget is derivable roughly; no calls, tokens, latency or dollars, and DEPS's extra rounds are not budget-matched. Matches the anchor-2 instance (call budget inferable, extra channel unpriced).

resolutions.reason: See rating reason: residual vs Inner Monologue-style feedback replanning overstated by the authors and not separated in Minecraft.
Anchors v2 partial-denominator clause (diamond/oracle denominators missing; 71 vs 69 task mismatch).
Headline comparison is model- and controller-matched against CaP; selector and rounds isolated; multi-LLM within-model gains. Confounds recorded do not leave the key gain unseparated.

Partial demo/eval overlap (2 of 69 tasks) plus robustness runs fits anchor 2; sol's extra deduction for 'privileged symbolic channels' is not applied because inventory is native game observation with a stated source.
+- is across-task dispersion, not run variance; no CI/paired test.
Round cap plus shared step caps make the call budget roughly derivable: anchor 2 instance.

K202 agreed. K104 adopted from sol: code-like goals are parsed onto a 262-goal controller vocabulary executed by a BC controller. R06 rejected: R06 samples candidate actions from a policy and lets a verifier pick; DEPS's selector ranks plan-parallel goals by predicted remaining horizon (efficiency, not correctness), which son55 itself called structural. Selector recorded as unassigned; son55's revision proposals kept pending.
